official.deadline_note: The application period for all seven participating higher education institutions runs from 1 June until 31 July; applications must be submitted to the master's course of your choice (maximum two), not to the DAAD, and each course names its own contact person.
official.application_cycle: 2027 intake: application period 1 June - 31 July 2026; selection by committee in October/November 2026; all applicants informed in writing after the selection process, expected December 2026/January 2027; funded courses start September/October 2027
official.status_note: The current DAAD announcement (05/2026, for the 2027 intake) states the application period ran from 1 June until 31 July 2026; selection is made by a selection committee in October/November 2026 comprising professors from the participating courses and DAAD representatives.
official.tuition_coverage_note: The DAAD announcement states: 'DAAD scholarship holders are exempt from paying tuition fees.'
benefits: Scholarship of currently EUR 992 per month for master's courses at German higher education institutions
DAAD scholarship holders are exempt from paying tuition fees
Fixed travel allowances (lump sums) for travel between Germany and the respective developing and emerging countries
Rent subsidies and family supplements, as applicable
A preceding German language course in Germany lasting up to 4 months; participation is mandatory
Accompanying support services from programme coordinators, events and seminars, close exchange with other international scholarship holders and interdisciplinary networking events
Study in small groups with special tutoring at the host institution and tailor-made workshops
eligibility: Very well qualified graduates with a first university degree (bachelor or equivalent)
Nationals of developing and emerging countries on the DAAD list of eligible countries
Above-average grades (upper third) in Social and Political Sciences, Law, Economics, Public Policy and Administration
Practical experience relevant for the programme (professional experience, internships, political or social commitment); specific requirements vary by master's course
Willing to actively contribute to the social and economic development of the home country or region
Both young graduates without professional experience and mid-career professionals may apply
The candidates' last university degree should not date back more than six years at the time of application (date of issue not before 1 January 2020)
Candidates who have spent more than the past 15 months in a country not listed on the DAC list are not eligible

Academic admission to the chosen master's course at one of the participating institutions
requirements: All applications must be submitted in English or German
Apply for a maximum of two master's courses listed in the announcement
Complete the DAAD 'Application Form' only once and indicate the selected master's course(s)
For two courses: rank the courses in order of preference in the motivation letter and submit the same letter of motivation to both courses
Submit the application directly to the master's course(s) of your choice with the required documents; scholarship applications must not be sent to the DAAD

Study at the chosen master's course in Germany after the preceding German language course

A single letter of motivation (max. two pages) with date of issue, covering academic, professional and personal reasons and justifying the ranking of the chosen courses
A curriculum vitae in reverse chronological order in europass format with date of issue; gaps of three months or more must be explained
Copies of higher education degree certificates with certified translations where the original is not in German or English
A copy of the full set of transcripts of records including an explanation of the grading system, with certified translation if needed

Confirmations of relevant professional experience or internships and/or proof of relevant political activities or community service, on headed paper with an original or code-certified digital signature, date of issue and stamp
A current written reference from the current employer or a university lecturer (for current students), on headed paper with original or code-certified digital signature, date of issue and stamp

selection_criteria: A conclusive account of your academic, professional and personal motivation for the study endeavour in Germany and for choosing and prioritising the master's courses
The motivation must clearly relate to the goals of the Helmut-Schmidt-Programme
Practical experience relevant to the programme (professional experience or internships, political activities or service to the community)
A first higher education degree completed with above-average grades (upper third)
Each master's course has its own selection criteria (degree, grades, language skills, practical experience) that must be met in addition to the DAAD's criteria
coverage: Fixed travel allowances (lump sums) for travel between Germany and the home region
Rent subsidies and family supplements, as applicable
German language course in Germany of up to 4 months before the master's studies
application_method: Read the DAAD selection criteria in the checklist carefully and take care of every point
Complete the DAAD application form once and indicate the selected master's course(s), maximum two
Rank first and second choice in the single motivation letter, submitted to both courses
Send the application directly to the master's course(s) with the required documents; applications sent to the DAAD are not forwarded and will not be returned
Nominated candidates are contacted by the DAAD by e-mail and asked to upload their full documents to the DAAD portal
official.application_route: Apply directly to one (or a maximum of two) participating master's courses with the DAAD application form and a single motivation letter ranking the choices - never send the application to the DAAD itself.
official.citizenship_residency: Open to graduates from developing and emerging countries on the DAAD list of eligible countries; candidates who have spent more than the past 15 months in a country not listed on the DAC list are not eligible.
official.international_eligibility: Yes - the scheme is open to candidates from developing and emerging countries on the DAAD list, whether young graduates or mid-career professionals.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Funded courses focus on Public Policy, Good Governance, International Relations, Public Management, Public Administration, Civil Society, Geo-Governance, Peace and Conflict Studies and Development and Socio-Economic Policies; the first degree should be in Social and Political Sciences, Law, Economics, Public Policy and Administration or a related field relevant to social, political and economic development.
official.duration: The selected master's course: 2 to 4 semesters depending on the course (Development and Governance at Duisburg-Essen: 2 semesters; the other six listed courses: 4 semesters), preceded by a German language course in Germany of up to 4 months; funded courses start September/October 2027.
official.description: The DAAD Helmut-Schmidt-Programme (known as Public Policy and Good Governance), funded by the Federal Foreign Office, supports future leaders from developing and emerging countries who want to promote democracy and social justice in their home regions, offering master's degrees in fields of particular importance for social, political and economic development.
official.program_type: Full master's scholarship for public policy and governance studies at selected German universities
official.english_requirement: Proof of English language skills is one of the required application documents; the requirements for language skills and the required language certificates vary depending on the respective master's course.

applicant_utility.summary: This is the Helmut-Schmidt route into public policy at seven German universities, and the application goes to the universities themselves - the DAAD never receives or forwards applications. You may pursue at most two courses, but you must use one DAAD application form and a single motivation letter that explicitly ranks the first and second choice and argues why each course advances you; the same letter goes to both courses. The money is a full package: currently EUR 992 per month, tuition exemption, health insurance, a study and research grant, lump-sum travel allowances, rent subsidies and family supplements where applicable, plus a mandatory German course of up to four months before you start. The 2027-intake window closed on 31 July 2026 with selection in October/November 2026, so the realistic target is the next June-July window for 2028 entry.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Graduates of social sciences, law, economics or administration with upper-third grades from a DAAD-listed developing or emerging country who want a policy or governance career and can meet both DAAD and specific course admission criteria.
application_readiness_checklist: Choose at most two courses and research each course's own admission requirements (degree, grades, language, experience) - meeting the DAAD criteria is necessary but not sufficient
Draft one motivation letter of maximum two pages that ranks both choices with clear reasons; write it before requesting references
Build a europass CV with the date of issue and explain any gap of three months or more
Line up a current reference on headed paper with an original or code-certified digital signature, date of issue and a stamp
Applicants from India and the People's Republic of China: start the APS Certificate early, as it must accompany the application
Organise certified translations of degree certificates and transcripts, plus an explanation of the grading system
common_rejection_risks: Applications addressed to more than two institutions, or without a clear and consistent prioritisation, are excluded from the selection
Sending files to the DAAD instead of the course - they are not forwarded, and uploaded originals are lost
Missing or incorrect information: the DAAD warns that applications may be rejected for formal reasons alone
A degree older than six years (issued before 1 January 2020) or more than 15 months recently spent in a non-DAC country
An unexplained existing master's degree, which requires a well-argued case for funding a second postgraduate degree
Uploading documents to the DAAD portal without being nominated by e-mail first
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: DAAD fee-free study, EUR 992 monthly, insurance, travel lumpsum and study grant cover tuition and standard living costs; personal extras, higher-rent top-ups beyond the published subsidy and family travel beyond the available supplements are self-funded.
document_audit: The checklist and criteria list must be ticked, hand-signed and dated with place of issue - a scanned signature page is required
Degree certificates and transcripts need certified translations unless already in German or English, and transcripts need the grading-system explanation
Experience confirmations must be on headed paper with an original or code-certified digital signature, a date of issue and a stamp - informal emails fail
Only one motivation letter covering both course choices is allowed; two different letters contradict the ranking and cause exclusion
The CV must carry a date of issue even though the europass template omits it
alerts: For the blended-learning Social Protection course at Bonn-Rhein-Sieg, the 4th semester is a mandatory online semester paid at a sur place rate of EUR 500 per month instead of the usual scholarship rate
German-language participation (up to four months) is mandatory and precedes the master's start in September/October 2027
The participating institution list has shrunk from eight to seven courses in recent years - verify the list each cycle
Nominated candidates upload full documents only after the DAAD contacts them by e-mail; premature uploads to the portal are discouraged
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Apply to one or two courses by the 31 July deadline with the DAAD form and a single ranked motivation letter; universities shortlist in October/November 2026; nominated candidates upload full documents to the DAAD portal and receive written results around December 2026/January 2027.
